Subject: kurila 1.5 released

kurila 1.5 released


Perl Kurila 1.5 has mainly changes to the Perl syntax, attempting
to make a cleaner syntax.

Highlights:
+ New dereference syntax: $ref->$, $ref->@, $ref->%, $ref->&, $ref->*
+ Method calls using $obj->?$name instead of $obj->$name
+ Improved Perl 5 to Kurila conversion script.
+ The bit operators &, |, ^, ~ are renamed to ^&^, ^|^, ^^^, ^~^.
+ use kurila 1.5 should be used to indicate kurila is required.
+ In m/$term[...]/ the [...] always indicates a subscript and never a
character class
+ Removal of the match once ?PATTERN? operator
+ The .. operator in scalar context will give an error.

Known bugs:
+ Documentation
+ Limited platform support

http://dev.tty.nl/static/kurila/doc/pod/kurila15delta.html
has a more complete list of the changes.



kurila 1.5 is released together with an additional 113 CPAN modules,
available together at:
http://dev.tty.nl/static/kurila/kurila-bundle-1.5.tar.gz

kurila 1.5 without the CPAN modules is available at:
http://dev.tty.nl/static/kurila/kurila-1.5_0.tar.gz
And should become available on CPAN.
Or use git to get the latest version:
cg-clone git://dev.tty.nl/perl#kurila



Perl Kurila is a dialect of Perl. With Perl 5 as ancestor it has a
solid base, but without the backwards compatibility
requirement of Perl 5, it is free to evolve into new directions.

A longer explanation of kurila is available at
http://dev.tty.nl/static/kurila/doc/pod/kurilaintro.html



Standing on the shoulders of a red giant to face the future.

p.s. I requested the creation of a cckrkk@perl.org mailing list, but it
isn't there yet.
